applies_why: This judge text treats the defender’s answers and the challenger’s press as competing chains and decides the collision as underdetermined rather than by checking whether one verse states the contrary.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: I weighed whether "weighs chain against chain by footing" requires an express footing comparison or merely forbids verse-by-verse disposition; the judge text speaks in chain-against-chain terms and does not apply a stating-verse test.
why: The judge text resolves the clash as one chain against another and does not use the retired requirement that a single pressed verse state the contrary in its own words.
